text:
A duplex came across the desk last month that looked perfect on paper.

Good rents. Solid neighborhood. ARV checked out. The investor was ready to write the offer that afternoon.

Then we ran debt service coverage ratio — net operating income divided by the annual mortgage payment. It came back at 1.02.

Most lenders want 1.20 or higher. At 1.02, one vacancy month or one surprise repair puts the property in the red.

The deal wasn't bad. The financing structure was. A larger down payment fixed the ratio and the lender approved it the second time.

Good rents don't mean a good deal until the debt fits the income.
